comparator.name: Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 ordinary generic Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences is verified as 60 EC compulsory first-year foundations + 60 EC compulsory second-year study + 14 EC final-year compulsory modern-drug-development and academic skills + 16 EC bachelor research (practical12, thesis3, presentation1) + 30 EC genuine approved open elective space = 180 EC. No named route is selected: the least specialised ordinary BFW pathway preserves the official minor/elective space independently of UCR fit. Pharmacy is an optional selective direction requiring at least80 EC and completed practical exercises; its five30-EC modules replace open space only for admitted participants and are not compulsory for all BFW students. Self-composed packages, other-institution minors and later changes need examination-board approval. Research entry requires all first-year units/propedeuse and second-year practical units; one outstanding practical may permit a restricted research offering depending on prior knowledge. The research period is continuous and may not be combined with other courses/practicals. All37 counted components occur once; the16-EC research parent is not added to its12/3/1 subparts.

core: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, disease mechanisms and experimental investigation
Drug targets, action in the human body, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, toxicity, safety and therapeutic use
Laboratory, statistical and evidence-synthesis methods for biomedical and pharmaceutical research
adjacent: Dose-response, pharmacological modelling, data analysis and machine learning for drug research
Medicinal chemistry, molecular design, synthesis and targeted drug delivery

trace: develops optimisation and constrained search methods for quantitative therapeutic-model and candidate-selection problems; it is not medicinal chemistry or molecular design
develops data cleaning, visualisation and project-based analysis for biomedical and drug-research measurements
implements regression, classification, resampling and clustering for prediction and pattern discovery in pharmaceutical and biomedical data
develops neural-network modelling and implementation for complex biological or treatment-response data without claiming dedicated cheminformatics
establishes Python programming, testing and computational problem-solving for reproducible biomedical-data and modelling workflows
establishes calculus and differential-equation methods used to represent concentration, response and dynamic biological processes
develops matrix, vector and eigenvalue methods for multivariable biological and pharmacological models
implements numerical equation solving, integration and differential equations for dynamic concentration-response and physiological models
extends calculus and differential equations to multivariable systems used in advanced quantitative pharmacology
studies differential-equation and state-space representations of linear systems as concrete tools for dynamic drug-response modelling
develops probability, estimation and simulation for uncertainty, dose-response evidence and biomedical measurement
studies disease frequency, risk, screening and causal evidence, supporting population-level assessment of therapeutic effectiveness and safety
connects anatomical structure with organ-system function and medical imaging, locating drug action and disease effects within the human body
directly studies drug targets, molecular interactions, pharmacokinetics, toxicity and quantitative concentration-response relationships
studies immune recognition, host-pathogen interactions and immunopathology as disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets
derives pathophysiology across organ systems from anatomy and physiology, providing the disease-mechanism basis for rational intervention
studies neurobiology, disorders, animal models, laboratory techniques and research ethics as one concrete biomedical application domain
studies neural mechanisms of perception and action, supplying organ-system function relevant to neuroactive drug effects without claiming neuropharmacology
introduces macromolecules, DNA, cells, signalling and physiology as the biological foundation for pharmacology and disease study
introduces brain and behavioural science plus experimental methods as the formal foundation for later treatment-evidence synthesis and neural applications
studies cellular structure, signalling, gene regulation and drug mechanisms, directly connecting molecular biology with therapeutic action
studies homeostasis, signalling and integrated organ-system physiology needed to understand drug effects in the human body
studies biomolecule chemistry, metabolism and molecular dysfunction, supplying the biochemical foundation while not replacing organic or medicinal chemistry
practises biochemical and molecular laboratory methods with proteins, DNA, bacteria, bioinformatics and antibiotic effects
studies molecular pathology, genetic disease, testing and treatment as mechanisms linking biological discovery to intervention
develops regression, multivariate analysis and experimental inference for biomedical and treatment-response evidence
performs systematic review and meta-analysis in R to estimate treatment effects and assess consistency across studies

alternatives.label: Molecular pharmacology, disease & therapeutic research
alternatives.concept: Study drug action through molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, human physiology, pharmacology, pathology, immunology and laboratory research, supported by statistics and quantitative modelling. Preserve specialist chemistry, synthesis and formulation gaps explicitly.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by molecular/physiological biology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and biomedical research methods; the label does not claim the missing pharmaceutical-chemistry sequence.
progression: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and six level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Life/health foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology, laboratory work and all advanced biomedical courses; biochemistry and physiology precede Pharmacology. Brain-and-behaviour foundations precede Perception & Action and the Advanced Research Seminar. Mathematical Methods precedes numerical methods, linear algebra and probability/statistics, while introductory data analysis precedes machine learning.

alternatives.label: Quantitative pharmacology & data-driven therapeutics
alternatives.concept: Retain molecular biology, physiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and laboratory research while prioritising mathematical systems, optimisation, machine learning and treatment-effect synthesis for quantitative drug development.
alternatives.labelReason: Four biological application courses are replaced by advanced calculus, systems, optimisation and neural-network study, creating a quantitatively focused therapeutic-research curriculum without claiming medicinal chemistry or pharmacometrics specialisation.
progression: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and eight level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Biological and mathematical gateways precede all dependent work; biochemistry and physiology precede Pharmacology. Introductory programming/data study precedes advanced optimisation and neural-network implementation, and introductory biomedical statistics precedes systematic review and meta-analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction. Functional Anatomy, Infection & Immunity, Neurobiology and Perception & Action are replaced by Advanced Calculus, Linear Systems, Optimisation Methods in AI and Neural Networks & Deep Learning. This is a substantive shift from biological-system applications to quantitative therapeutic modelling, not threshold-filling substitution.

candidates.label: Quantitative pharmacology, dose-response and data-driven therapeutic research

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass evidence, course-content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. A third medicinal-chemistry and targeted-delivery route is not defensible because the workbook lacks general and organic chemistry sequences, medicinal chemistry, analytical pharmaceutical chemistry, synthesis, formulation, drug-delivery technology and chemistry laboratories. Molecular biology and biochemistry are not relabelled as those missing subjects.

blocks: Both establish cellular and molecular foundations; UCR also introduces genetics, signalling and physiology.
Both directly study cellular molecular mechanisms and biochemical processes; the external course remains specifically pharmaceutical in context.
Both study human physiological systems; UCR does not reproduce the external histology component.
Both directly study biomolecule chemistry and metabolism; UCR does not provide the external organic-chemistry sequence.
Both involve biochemical laboratory methods; UCR additionally covers DNA, bacteria and bioinformatics and does not claim pharmaceutical analysis.
Both directly address molecular genetics; UCR integrates genetics with pathology and treatment.
Drug action, disease and therapeutic evidence
Both directly study human anatomy; UCR emphasises structure/function and imaging rather than the full external biomedical sequence.
Both directly study pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, drug targets, dose-response and toxicity.
Both directly study immune mechanisms; UCR additionally emphasises infection and immunopathology.
Both directly study disease mechanisms and organ-system pathology.
Both develop machine-learning methods; UCR supplies a general data-science course rather than pharmaceutical applications.
Both provide mathematical foundations for pharmaceutical and biomedical science; UCR focuses on calculus and differential equations.
UCR numerical equation solving and differential equations supply important modelling methods, but not the external pharmacological application sequence.
Both provide probability and statistical foundations for scientific evidence.
Both develop statistical analysis of biomedical or human data; UCR emphasises multivariate and experimental methods.
External specialist chemistry, development, research and elective space
Both support academic development; UCR PPD also includes personal, civic and collaborative formation.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, laboratory work and quantitative research. They do not reproduce Leiden’s organic and medicinal chemistry, drug synthesis, pharmaceutical analysis, formulation/biopharmacy laboratories or complete drug-development sequence, and therefore represent related biomedical routes rather than a full Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences curriculum.
